archetype: Mono-red Goblin swarm with a storm half bolted on. deck-audit establishes no archetype, so the BASE targets apply and no override was used; strategic_frame.json calls it "Mono-red Goblin swarm with a storm half bolted to it". The measured engine agrees with that ordering: the token target assembles 60.0% at mean turn 3.184, the Zada target 66.3% at mean turn 5.243, the storm target 26.5% at mean turn 4.914. Swarm is the floor, storm is the ceiling.
verdict: It functions, and five checker-passed stacks record what its board actually does. Mana is at or over target on every mana axis and the turn-3 land drop lands 90%; the reminder-text fix did not create a mana problem, it narrowed a cushion from 7 sources above the Karsten yardstick to 4. What limits it is conversion. The ceiling assembles 26.5% because the storm target is an AND of two independent four-card groups, and the 60% swarm floor that has to carry the other games does not close — the pod run's median combat damage dealt is 6.5 against 28.5 taken over a mean 16.8 rounds, and the deck's ten reach cards are filed by the taxonomy as removal, which is why threat-density reads 2.

gaps: There is no deck_recon.json for this deck (deck-audit reports recon present: false), so nothing here is grounded in what other Zada or Goblin-storm lists actually run. Every add is corpus-mined, not meta-sourced.

There is no captain's log and no log_annotations.json for goblin-storm — `deck-notes list` returns no entries. Nothing in this diagnosis is grounded in a game the pilot played; the only table evidence is one 20-game Forge run.

That run is AI on all four seats, and its own assumptions block quotes Forge's docs saying the AI is "pretty bad for most combo decks". A 1-of-20 win rate (ci95 [0.009, 0.236]) is therefore not a measurement of this deck's ceiling. The figures I lean on — combat damage dealt and taken, first attack turn, token attackers — are structural rather than skill-bound, but they are still AI-piloted.

The run was against giada-angels, vito and baylen-tokens, which are pod seats, but the deck has never been simulated against a second pod, so nothing here separates 'this deck is slow' from 'this table is fast'.

deck-audit's mana-sources axis names Impulsive Pilferer and Storm-Kiln Artist among five persistent producers, while the corrected mana_analysis.json excludes both from its producer list. Both read card_roles.json, which tags each ramp:dork as well as ramp:treasure. The two commands disagree and I have not picked one; the residual is in the roles file, not in either command.

mana_analysis.json still credits Goblin Burrows and Kher Keep as red land sources. Their only mana ability is "{T}: Add {C}"; the red comes from a colour-identity fallback fed by their {1}{R} activation costs. I enumerated all 15 land entries and these are the two affected, so the true repeatable red land count is 31, not 33. The axis figure carried above is the audit's and is unchanged.

bracket_report.json carries no target field and deck-audit reports it as not stamped with the current decklist sha, so 'is this deck inside its intended bracket' is unanswered — only the floor of 4 is computed.

card_roles.json classifies 87.3% of this deck; ten entries have no role at all (Chaos Warp, Crimson Wisps, Daring Discovery, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Past in Flames, Reliquary Tower, Renegade Tactics, Spreading Insurrection, Wild Ride). Several are load-bearing: grepping all 79 entries for destroy / exile / counter target / return target / gain control returns fifteen cards, of which Goblin Trashmaster and Vandalblast answer artifacts, Spreading Insurrection answers a creature, and the remainder act on your own library or graveyard — which leaves Chaos Warp, role-less, as the deck's answer to an opposing enchantment or land. Every role-derived axis here is a floor rather than a count.
deck-facts reports 42 synergy edges falling inside this deck, but the synergy graph is a format-wide top-10 shortlist and not a fit score, so no claim in this document rests on it.

Four combo lines are contained in the deck. One — Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage — is verified by stack 005. The three Krenko lines were examined by stack 004, also checker-passed, which found they do not produce their advertised infinite here because Zada is the commander and a sacrificed Krenko stays in the graveyard.

Roaming Throne is counted as one of the two protection copies on the strength of ward {2}; its actual job is doubling a chosen creature type's triggers, and no artifact settles which type it should name or whether Zada's copy trigger is doubled.
